post.title: Hephaestus: Computing Age Film
post.hook: Abacus to reasoning machines, drawn as engraved plates in a 9:16 film.
post.summary: A vertical HyperFrames film, HEPHAESTUS, that walks through five thousand years of computing as engraved diagram plates. It has a generated build, a storyboard of 7 chapters, and rendered snapshots.
post.writeup:
## What it is
HEPHAESTUS is a silent vertical film (1080x1920) on the history of computing, built with HyperFrames. The brief set a target of about 120s; the storyboard settles on 110s. It is modeled on the viral "Prometheus" video: engraved plates drawing themselves on, a year ruler along the bottom, a running ops/second index, Latin chapter cards and chromatic aberration on every cut.

## Why
The message: "Computing is one accelerating project: from counting stones to thinking machines." The film is meant to be cut to music added later, so scenes sit on a steady grid.

## How it works
The film is generated. `src/film.mjs` holds chapters, scenes and timing, and `src/build.mjs` writes `index.html`. `src/runtime.js` runs one paused GSAP timeline, plus a single scene-ticker that computes continuous effects (year counter, grain, flicker, chroma) as pure functions of time, so seeking is deterministic. Diagrams are layered SVGs (L-con, L-main, L-detail, L-acc, L-lbl), each written by a small plain-Node script. Paper and grain textures come from a seeded Python script.

## Structure
Seven chapters, from CALCULUS (abacus, Antikythera) through MACHINA, ANALYTICA, LOGOS, SILICIUM and RETE to MENS (deep learning, Transformer, reasoning machines), then a one-word card: COGITO. The mechanical age (I to III) sits on aged paper; the electric age (IV to VII) is gold on black. Scene length shrinks from 5.5s to 4.0s per chapter, so the film itself accelerates.

## State
Snapshots and a contact sheet exist, and eight diagram scripts are present (abacus to ENIAC), so the film renders. Music is still to be added.

## Open questions
Do the later chapters (silicon, net, mind) need hand-built plates as detailed as the first eight?
